# Cunda Sutta (Snp 1.5 (PTS Snp 16))

**ID:** Snp 1.5 (PTS Snp 16)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Cunda Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

These four classes comprise the path-conqueror (*maggajina*), the path-teacher (*maggadesaka*), the path-liver (*maggajīvin*), and the path-corrupter (*maggadūsin*); S. M. Katre points out that this scheme reflects degrees of spiritual attainment rather than sectarian affiliation [Katre 1931]. G. C. Pande notes that although the discourse is entirely centered on the concept of the path (*maggo*), it makes no mention of the eightfold division of the path [Pande 1974]. Metrically, K. R. Norman observes that verses 83–90 are composed in the Aupacchandasaka metre, except for verse 88a, which is Vaitālīya [Norman 1997-2001].

 DharmaNexus agrees with this cross-tradition alignment, identifying extensive textual matches with the Sanskrit *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra* as well as Tibetan translations of the *Vinaya-kṣudrakavastu* (D 6), the *Abhidharmakośopāyikā-ṭīkā* (D 4094), and the *Vyākhyāyuktisūtrakhaṇḍaśata* (D 4060) [DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus records 13 matching segments shared with its commentary, the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
